name: Lode
subtitle: the homing planet
story: Everyone on Lode is born with a little iron in the blood, and it points to where they were born. Every December, the whole planet follows it home. Most of them were born in the hospital, which is a supermarket now, so every December thirty thousand people come home to aisle three. Sister Bridget delivered every one of them. She's on the tills now.
hook: A planet for people who go home for Christmas.

episode.opener:
On Lode, your blood
points home.

beats.text:
Home, meaning
where you were born.

Every December,
everyone follows it home.

Most people were born
in the hospital.

beats.note: turn line, a push in on the same building

beats.text:
I tried it.
Mine points straight down.

Most of the year,
it's quiet.

Then it's December.
Thirty thousand people
come home to aisle three.
beats.note: identical camera, one thing changed: the queue

beats.text:
Sister Bridget delivered
every one of them.

episode.caption:
The whole queue was born in that shop.

Lode is a snowy, hilly planet of 52,000 people, and none of them has ever been lost. You're born with a little iron in the blood, and it points, very gently, at the spot where you arrived. Sat-navs never caught on. In December the whole planet sets off home, and most of it ends up at the big supermarket on the ring road, which was the hospital until 1988. Midwives on Lode don't really retire.

The man on the next till asked where mine pointed. I said down. He went very quiet and gave me a free bag.

(You have iron in your blood too: three or four grams of it, most of it in your red cells. Ours doesn't point anywhere. We go home anyway.)

Where does your iron point?

first_comment: Bridget: Thirty thousand home this year. I've told every one of them to stand up straight.

beats.text:
For most people,
that's the hospital.

At Christmas, thirty thousand
come home to aisle three.
